reviews.notes: Accurately represents Arjuna's query comparing devotees of the revealed personal God with worshippers of the unrevealed, unbodied Absolute.
Directly matches Krishna's judgment that those who fix their minds on Him with steadfast faith and constant devotion are the most perfect yogis.
Faithfully renders the attributes of the Akshara: Invisible, Unrevealed, Unnamed, Unthinkable, All-pervading, and Immovable.
Matches mastering the senses, remaining even-minded everywhere, delighting in the welfare of all beings, and attaining the Lord.
Accurately conveys the greater hardship (kleśo'dhikataras) of the unmanifest path for embodied mortals.
Directly matches dedicating all actions to Krishna, holding Him supreme, and meditating with unswerving devotion.
Faithfully renders the Lord swiftly delivering those whose minds are absorbed in Him from the ocean of mortal existence (mṛtyusaṃsārasāgarāt).
Accurately represents fixing heart and mind on Krishna alone, dwelling with Him beyond doubt.
Matches abhyāsayoga: seeking to attain the Lord through constant, steadfast practice if unable to fix the mind firmly at once.
Directly matches performing works dedicated to the Lord (matkarmaparamo bhava) to achieve perfection if unable to practice meditation.
Faithfully reflects renouncing the fruits of all labor (sarvakarmaphalatyāga) with self-control as the refuge for the faint of heart.
Accurately preserves the graded hierarchy: knowledge excels mechanical practice, meditation excels knowledge, renunciation of fruits excels meditation, bringing immediate Peace.
Faithfully renders adveṣṭā sarvabhūtānāṃ maitraḥ karuṇa eva ca: hating no creature, friendly, compassionate, free from egoism and pride, patient in joy and grief.
Matches ever content, self-controlled, of firm resolve, mind and intellect dedicated to Krishna ('That man I love!').
Accurately conveys neither troubling the world nor troubled by it, freed from joy, anger, fear, and anxiety ('That man I love!').
Matches dwelling quiet-eyed (anapekṣa [FN#25]), pure, dexterous, impartial, and renouncing selfish undertakings.
Faithfully renders neither rejoicing nor hating, grieving nor hankering, renouncing both good and evil, full of devotion.
Directly matches remaining equal to friend and foe, in honour and ignominy, in heat and cold, and in pleasure and pain.
Accurately captures equanimity under praise or blame (tulyanindāstutir), silent, content with whatever comes, homeless, steady in mind.
Accurately concludes the chapter: those who follow this immortal doctrine of devotion (dharmyāmṛtam) with faith and surrender are exceedingly dear to the Lord.

chapterFindings: Chapter 12 translation provides complete 1-to-1 canonical coverage across all 20 verses without omissions or mergers.
Arnold structures the concluding portrait of the ideal devotee with the recurring cadence 'That man I love!', faithfully reflecting the repeated Sanskrit refrain 'sa me priyaḥ'.
Footnote [FN#25] is accurately positioned on the translation of 'anapeksha' in verse 12.16.
